response.sql:
WITH order_counts_by_type AS (
  SELECT 
    o.ordertune,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oe.ordersmark) as order_count
  FROM orderexecutions oe
  INNER JOIN orders o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
),
total_orders AS (
  SELECT SUM(order_count) as total FROM order_counts_by_type
),
shares_by_type AS (
  SELECT 
    oct.ordertune,
    oct.order_count,
    oct.order_count::float / to.total as share,
    AVG(oct.order_count::float / to.total) OVER () as avg_share
  FROM order_counts_by_type oct
  CROSS JOIN total_orders to
),
above_avg_types AS (
  SELECT 
    ordertune,
    order_count,
    share,
    avg_share,
    share - avg_share as excess
  FROM shares_by_type
  WHERE share > avg_share
)
SELECT
  SUM(order_count) as total_count,
  AVG(share) as avg_share,
  AVG(excess) as avg_excess
FROM above_avg_types

assumptions.assumption: "Executed orders" means unique orders of each type that have at least one execution, counted via COUNT(DISTINCT oe.ordersmark). The phrasing "how many executed orders each order type has" emphasizes orders (plural noun) not execution events, supporting this reading.
At least one order type has a share strictly above the overall average share. If no types exceed the average, the result is entirely NULL.

alternatives.interpretation: "Executed orders" refers to execution records themselves (all fills/partial fills per order type), not unique orders. Count total executions per type using COUNT(*) rather than counting distinct orders.
alternatives.sql:
WITH execution_counts_by_type AS (
  SELECT 
    o.ordertune,
    COUNT(*) as execution_count
  FROM orderexecutions oe
  INNER JOIN orders o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
),
total_executions AS (
  SELECT SUM(execution_count) as total FROM execution_counts_by_type
),
shares_by_type AS (
  SELECT 
    ecbt.ordertune,
    ecbt.execution_count,
    ecbt.execution_count::float / te.total as share,
    AVG(ecbt.execution_count::float / te.total) OVER () as avg_share
  FROM execution_counts_by_type ecbt
  CROSS JOIN total_executions te
),
above_avg_types AS (
  SELECT 
    ordertune,
    execution_count,
    share,
    avg_share,
    share - avg_share as excess
  FROM shares_by_type
  WHERE share > avg_share
)
SELECT
  SUM(execution_count) as total_count,
  AVG(share) as avg_share,
  AVG(excess) as avg_excess
FROM above_avg_types
